newsitem.title: USA: P&G, Hoechst Marion in Actonel pact.
newsitem.headline: P&G, Hoechst Marion in Actonel pact.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co and and Hoechst Marion Roussel, the pharmaceutical company of Hoechst AG, said on Monday they formed a global alliance to commercialize Procter's bone health therapy Actonel, a bisphosphonate therapy in phase III clinical trials.

The companies said they would work together to complete clinical studies, obtain regulatory approvals and develop sales and marketing plans to launch Actonel for osteoporosis and other bone diseases in all countries except Japan.
The agreement was effective immediately and would last until 2015, they said.
As part of the agreement, Hoechst Marion Roussel would make milestone payments to Procter & Gamble to help offset P&G's investment to date in this therapy, they said.
The companies said they would share future revenues and costs for Actonel but no other financial terms were disclosed.

John Pepper, chairman and chief executive of Procter & Gamble said: "Hoechst Marion Roussel has a significant worldwide presence and a broad global distribution network, enabling us to bring this breakthrough new therapy to more patients globally than we could have alone, and help ensure we achieve maximum commercial success."
Hoechst Marion's chief executive officer Richard Markham said the company had placed more emphasis on research and development in the area of bone health and Actonel would support this focus.
Actonel is an advanced third generation bisphosphonate under study for all major forms of osteoporosis across a broad range of patients, the companies said.
It works by inhibiting the bone resorption process in osteoporotic patients that progressively thins and weakens bones, they said.
The companies said industry analysts expected the global osteoporosis market to reach $5 billion in sales by 2005 with up to 200 million patients at risk over the next 10 years.
Consumer products company Procter & Gamble develops and markets its own pharmaceutical products in North America and Europe as well as marketing consumer brands in 140 countries.
Hoeschst Marion Roussel said it had critical mass in Asia, Latin America, Africa and Eastern Europe which would ensure patient access to Actonel in these markets.
